column4: A very elderly & very sick woman came into the store during shift. She wanted help with the t-shirts. It was apparent that she was in really poor physical health, was slurring her words and seemed really physically exhausted. She couldn't stand up right and eventually needed Kaew & I to support her standing & walking. We sat her down, and she said she had just received chemotherapy earlier that day. She could not stand up right without hunching over as if to pass out/faint. She declined us calling a taxi, ambulence, and did not want us to call anyone to help her. She adamantly stated that did not want to go back to the hospital, even though she was in no physical condition to be out & about. Left store of her own volition. She later returned during Vanessa's closing shift, and again was very difficult, and stayed with Vanessa 30 minutes past close time. During this time, she also denied Vanessa calling an ambulence, a taxi or calling someone to assist the woman. This woman put all of us into an uncomfortable position of duty of care for someone severely in denial about needing assistance. Despite this woman's clear poor physical stature, she was adamant that she didn't need any help, making this a difficult & uncomfortable situation to navigate.

column4: An asian man of tanned skin around his 40s around 160 cm entered the store and came and sat down behind the counter. He sat down for a few minutes and then mimicked and mocked a customer during a transaction. Limey questioned him, 'Are you just waiting for someone?' He replied 'yes' and began to say something incomprehensively. It seemed like he was waiting for someone in the store. Limey went to question the lady who just exited the change room and if she knew the man, and she said no. Liz was serving the counter when the man approached her and said "I like your tattoos", Liz thanked the man and continued on with the transaction. After this transaction finished he walked toward liz and began to wrap his arms around her whilst saying "goodbye", "i'll see you soon". Liz froze up but thanked and farewelled the man as there were still customers in line. The customers in line appeared quite shocked and the man then continued talking to Liz. As he wished Liz a "Merry Christmas", Yue was coming back off her break from the change rooms. She met Limey at the sale rack in the kids section behind the Christmas and Limey said "there is a weird man at the counter. we have no idea who he is." Yue then walks up to the counter, to see the man standing very awkwardly next to Liz. At this moment, Yue has witnessed him say "I'll see you soon, merry christmas." Limey then came to the register shortly after Yue, and the man lingered behind the counter for a few moments before finally leaving the store. After he left the store, there was a starnge screaming/yelling noise coming from the doorway of the store on the streetfront, which attracted the attention of customers in store. It may have been the strange man interracting with a member of the public outside. The man's behaviour, facial expressions & eyes were abmornal. He may have been drunk/high/on substances.
